title: Model version lifecycle cutover and pin safeguard protocol
creator: Priya Shah
description: Define and implement a repeatable cutover and deprecation protocol for model versions that prioritizes customer continuity and minimizes surprise. This issue covers: (1) automated pin-safeguard checks that prevent accidental mass-upgrades for pinned customers, (2) staged public notices and in-console guidance for migration, (3) publication of updated performance profiles and compatibility notes, and (4) telemetry and rollback hooks to detect and mitigate customer regressions after a version sunset or cutover.
acceptance_criteria: A. Pin-safeguard: Console and API reject bulk replace operations that would override explicit model_version pins for any customer without a two-step confirmation and audit log entry.
B. Notice cadence: Notices are published to the console and sent to affected accounts at milestones: 90d, 60d, 30d, 14d, 7d, 1d before enforced cutover.
C. Migration guide templates: For each model family we publish a one-page migration doc (compatibility matrix, sample prompt deltas, token cost delta, recommended fallback variants).
D. Telemetry: A dashboard tracks pinned users, migration intent signals (SDK warnings, check-pin API calls), and post-cutover error/regression rate within 72 hours with alerting thresholds.
E. Rollback/fallback: Runtime supports automatic downgrade routing to the previous stable variant for 48 hours post-cutover if error rate exceeds threshold.

rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dry-run): Apply to internal and 3 opt-in beta orgs for one model family (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (soft notices): Start sending 90d + 60d notices for upcoming scheduled cutovers (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (hard safeguards): Enforce pin-safeguard on new bulk operations and enable routing fallback hooks (1 week)
Phase 3 (general availability): Turn on full notice cadence and publish migration guides for top 8 model families (2 weeks)

notes: Key trade-offs: stricter safeguards reduce risk but increase friction for orgs intentionally replacing many pins (e.g., infra refresh). Provide an override path with audit and two-step confirmation for org admins. Metric priorities: pinned-orgs left behind, migration success rate, post-cutover error/regression.
risks: Customers with large fleets of pinned endpoints may be delayed in adopting security-critical updates if override UX is too hidden.
Telemetry gaps could cause false-positive rollback triggers if metrics are noisy during regional infra events.
Operational burden: Support will get spike in migration assistance requests during first two release cycles.
